objectives: This course introduces students to linguistic analysis using contemporary digital tools and authentic food discourse data. Students will explore how linguistic patterns, meanings, identities, and social relationships are constructed through approaches such as discourse analysis and corpus-informed analysis. Digital tools including concordance tools, word clouds, frequency analysis, Google Trends, and AI-assisted analysis will be introduced as methods for investigating language use. Through project-based learning and hands-on data analysis, students will critically examine both the possibilities and limitations of digital tools and AI in linguistic inquiry.
content:
1		Introduction: What Is Linguistic Analysis?
2		Language, culture, and meaning
3		Collecting digital data
4		Word frequency and word clouds
5		Concordance and collocation
6		Food, identity, and evaluation
7		Digital discourse and social media
8		Project proposal workshop
9		Midterm project check-in
10		Trends and language change
11		AI as a linguistic tool
12		Human analysis vs AI analysis
13		Visualizing linguistic patterns
14		Project workshop
15		Final project presentations
16		Final project due

This syllabus is tentative and subject to revision.

Jurafsky. 2015. The Language of Food
Readings and worksheets provided by the instructor
